title: Fragmenting Bulk Hydrogels and Processing into Granular Hydrogels for Biomedical Applications
protocol: Predetermine desired concentrations of polymer, crosslinker, and initiators for the bulk hydrogel formulation.
Dissolve NorHA (2 wt.%), DTT (6 mM), and Irgacure D-2959 (0.05 wt.%) in PBS within a microcentrifuge tube to prepare the hydrogel precursor solution.
Transfer 1 mL of the hydrogel precursor solution into a 3 mL syringe using a 1,000 µL pipette.
Load the prepared hydrogel precursor solution into the syringe barrel with a tip cap attached.
Hold the syringe barrel with hydrogel precursor solution in one hand.
Return the syringe plunger to the opening of the back of the syringe barrel.
Gently push the plunger into the barrel to seal the opening at the back of the syringe barrel.
Carefully hold the plunger and syringe barrel together to ensure the back of the syringe barrel is sealed with the plunger.
Invert the syringe such that the plinger is facing down, and the tip cap is now facing up.
Remove the tip cap and gently push the plunger into the syringe barrel until all the air is removed from the syringe.
Reattach the tip cap to the syringe.
Ensure that the hydrogel precursor solution is secured within the 3 mL syringe with a tip cap.
Form a bulk hydrogel within the 3 mL syringe.
Wear UV-protectant eyeglasses prior to turning on the UV lamp.
Enclose the lamp area to protect others from UV light.
Calibrate the UV spot cure lamp to a light intensity of 10 mW/cm² using a radiometer.
Place the 3 mL syringe loaded with the hydrogel precursor solution under the UV spot cure lamp.
Expose NorHA hydrogel precursor solution to UV light for 5 min at an intensity of 10 mW/cm².
Flip the syringe halfway through the photocrosslinking period to ensure complete crosslinking within the syringe.
Turn off the UV lamp and remove the syringe from the curing setup.
Pull back the plunger to observe the hydrogel moving as a solid block, confirming complete photocrosslinking.
Remove the plunger from an empty 3 mL syringe.
Secure a tip cap to the Luer-Lock on the empty syringe.
Remove the tip cap from the syringe containing the photocrosslinked bulk hydrogel.
Line up the top of the hydrogel syringe with the opening of the barrel on the empty syringe.
Extrude the bulk hydrogel through the syringe opening into the barrel of the empty syringe.
Discard the now-empty syringe that formerly contained the hydrogel properly into waste.
Hold the syringe containing the extruded hydrogel such that the tip cap is facing down and the barrel opening is facing up.
Add 1.5 mL of PBS to the syringe barrel using a 1,000 µL pipette.
Align the plunger with the barrel opening to create a seal.
Invert the syringe so the plunger faces down and the tip cap faces up while holding the plunger and barrel together securely.
Invert multiple times to mix fragmented hydrogel with PBS added thoroughly.
Hold the syringe such that the tip cap is facing up and the plunger is facing down.
Remove the tip cap from the syringe.
Very gently push the plunger upwards to remove any air from inside the syringe.
Secure a blunt-tip 18 G needle to the syringe containing the fragmented hydrogel and PBS.
Remove the plunger from a fresh 3 mL syringe and secure a tip cap to the empty syringe barrel.
Extrude the fragmented hydrogel suspension through the 18 G needle into the back of the empty syringe barrel.
Discard the empty syringe and needle into the proper sharps waste stream.
Hold the syringe containing the fragmented hydrogel such that the tip cap is facing down, and the barrel opening is facing up.
Align the syringe plunger with the opening of the barrel to create a seal.
Invert the syringe so the plunger faces down and the tip cap faces up while holding the plunger and syringe barrel together.
Hold the syringe such that the tip cap is facing up and the plunger is facing down.
Remove the tip cap.
Gently push the plunger upwards to remove any air from the inside of the syringe.
Repeat steps with a 23 G needle.
Repeat steps with a 27 G needle.
Repeat steps with a 30 G needle.
Extrude the fragmented hydrogel suspension into microcentrifuge tubes using the 30 G needle.
Wash and isolate the fragmented hydrogel suspension.
Spin down the fragmented microgel suspension at 5,000 x g for 5 min using a microcentrifuge.
Remove the supernatant with a pipette.
Add 1 mL of PBS to each microcentrifuge tube containing fragmented microgels.
Vortex the mixture for 5-10 seconds.
Repeat centrifuging and washing with PBS three times.
Combine 20 µL of fragmented microgel suspension with 180 µL of PBS to create a dilute fragmented microgel suspension.
Vortex the mixture thoroughly to mix.
Transfer 50 µL of the diluted fragmented microgel suspension to a glass microscope slide.
Acquire images of fluorescently-labeled microgels using an epifluorescent microscope at 4x or 10x zoom.
Open the acquired images in ImageJ.
Select Analyze > Set Measurements, and check Area, Shape Descriptors, and Feret's Diameter.
Click OK to confirm settings.
Convert the image type to 8-bit by selecting Image > Type > 8-bit.
Adjust the threshold using Image > Adjust > Threshold such that microgels are covered by a red mask while the background remains black.
Apply the threshold adjustment.
If any microgels overlap slightly, use the Pencil Tool to draw a thin (<5 pixels) black line between overlapping microgels.
Select Analyze Particles.
Set Size (pixel²) from 50 to Infinity.
Set Circularity to 0.00-1.00.
Select Show Outlines from the Dropdown menu.
Check Display Results.
Check Exclude on Edges.
Check Include Holes.
Click OK.
Copy results into a spreadsheet.
Determine equivalent circular diameter for each particle.
Obtain image scale in µm/pixel.
Create column to convert area of each microgel from pixel² to µm².
Use area in µm² to determine the equivalent circular diameter of the microgel in µm.
Convert Feret's diameters to a unit of µm using the µm/pixel scale.
Resuspend microgels in 1 mL of PBS after removing PBS supernatant from the last washing step.
Spin down the fragmented hydrogel suspension at 18,000 x g for 5 min.
Remove the PBS supernatant.
Scoop the fragmented granular hydrogel out of the microcentrifuge tube using a metal spatula and transfer it into an empty syringe barrel.
Use a pipette tip to assist in transferring the granular hydrogel into the syringe.
Return the plunger to the syringe.
Load the fragmented granular hydrogel into the syringe, ready for use.
Assemble the vacuum-driven filtration apparatus by securing a Buchner funnel inside of a filter flask and placing the filter adapter between them.
Connect tubing from the filter flask to a vacuum line.
Place a membrane filter (0.22 µm) in the Buchner funnel cup.
Turn on the vacuum line by opening the dial valve.
Test the connection by pipetting ~0.5 mL of PBS onto the membrane filter and observe that all the PBS goes through the filter and collects in the bottom of the filter flask.
Turn on the vacuum line and ensure a complete seal.
Vortex the fragmented hydrogel suspension in PBS.
Transfer the fragmented hydrogel suspension onto the membrane filter (0.22 µm) using a 1,000 µL pipette.
Wait for approximately 30 seconds for the vacuum to pull PBS out of the fragmented hydrogel suspension.
Turn off the vacuum line.
Obtain a fresh 3 mL syringe and remove the plunger.
Scoop the fragmented granular hydrogel from the filter using a metal spatula and transfer it into the back of the empty syringe barrel.
Return the plunger to the syringe.
Load the fragmented granular hydrogel into the syringe, and it is now ready for use.
Place a membrane filter on the vacuum filtration apparatus.
Use a pipette to transfer fragmented microgel suspension onto the filter.
Pull the vacuum and wait for microgels to jam and form a granular hydrogel.
Turn off the vacuum and remove fragmented granular hydrogel using a metal spatula.
Transfer granular hydrogel to the syringe using a metal spatula.
Save the CAD file in ".stl" format.
Upload the .stl file to the 3D printing software by selecting the load button or File > Load.
Navigate to the Slicer panel and select Slic3r as the slicer option.
Adjust settings such as nozzle diameter, layer height, print speed, and extrusion rate based on ink characterization and desired outcomes.
Set nozzle diameter to match an 18 G needle (inner diameter of 838 µm).
Set layer height to 1 mm.
Set print speed to 8 mm/s.
Set flow rate to 9 µL/s.
Adjust numerical values of parameters by ±20% if necessary, to account for variations in the properties of granular hydrogel inks.
Remove the tip cap from the syringe and replace it with a needle of choice.
Load the prepared syringe containing fragmented granular hydrogels into the printing platform of the 3D printer.
Load the G-Code file prepared during the planning phase into the 3D printing software.
Navigate to the Print Preview panel in the software and press Print.
Expose the printed fragmented granular hydrogel constructs to UV light for photocrosslinking once deposition is complete.
Wash the processed sample in PBS three times.
